$comment: P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS): the runnable witness that `extern` written AFTER the other declaration specifiers PARSES AND MEANS what the references mean by it. C 6.7.1 makes the specifiers an unordered SET; until P53 DSS accepted `extern inline`/`extern __inline` and refused `inline extern`/`__inline extern` with error[P_NoAlternativeMatched], because `extern` was the HEAD of its own file-scope declaration rule. gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x`, clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23` and MSVC 19.51.36252 `/std:clatest`, probed SEPARATELY 2026-09-02, accept every ordering. ★★ IT PINS MEANING, NOT PARSING: C99 6.7.4p7 exempts an inline definition carrying `extern` from the no-external-definition rule, so the two orders must both EMIT the body — ✔MEASURED with `nm` on gcc and clang, `extern inline int p(int){…}` and `inline extern int p(int){…}` each give `T p` while a bare `inline int p(int){…}` gives `U p` and fails to link against a sibling TU that calls it. Identical symbol state ⇒ same meaning. ✔MEASURED on DSS at x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec: `nm` (llvm-nm over the PE) shows `T payload_a` and `T payload_b` in cu_a's object and `U sharedCounter`, and the image exits 42 at baseline AND at --config=release. ★ ARITHMETIC NAMES THE FAILING HALF, because the failure is SILENT otherwise: cu_b carries WEAK fallbacks, so a wrongly-suppressed definition still compiles, still links and emits ZERO diagnostics while the fallback quietly wins. 33 + 2 + 7 = 42 both correct; 10 = payload_a lost; 41 = payload_b lost; 9 = both lost. ★★ `sharedCounter` CARRIES THE NON-DEFINING HALF — the silent miscompile P53's first pass measured and refused to ship. With the grammar merge ALONE, `dsscp` printed `warning[H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier]: 'extern' is not a recognized linkage specifier` and EXITED 0, so every extern OBJECT became a TENTATIVE DEFINITION emitting storage in its own TU; binding cu_b's 7 across the TU boundary is impossible if cu_a defined its own. ★ `die` pins the TWO-LEADING-SPECIFIER form `_Noreturn inline extern void die(int);` — accepted by all three references, so a repair admitting only ONE specifier before `extern` would still have been below the union. RED-ON-DISABLE (REMOVE direction), ✔EXERCISED P53: delete the `"extern": {"nonDefining": true, …}` entry from topLevelDecl's `linkageSpecifiers` in c.lang.json and this example FAILS IN BOTH RUNNERS while inline_c99_extern_gnu_spellings — the same 6.7.4p7 mechanism in the ALREADY-WORKING order — stays GREEN, which is the control that says the mutant hit the non-defining fact and not the inline machinery.
